Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo this week. Kevin and I reviewed the feature list and we
need help deciding whether to move to a higher tier or stay on our current plan and
buy additional seats/add-ons. Our main questions:
- If we move up one tier, which features are immediately enabled vs. gated behind

- Is there a blended discount if we commit to a 12-month term but only need the
  higher tier for specific workloads (e.g., nightly batch inference)?
- Lastly, do you offer a one-time migration credit to help offset migration work?

Hi Emma — thanks for the doc and great questions. I sketched three concrete paths
below and attached a simple XLS that shows ballpark deltas. Quick summary up front:

1) Tier lift (Standard -> Premium) — best if you need native model variants,
   higher RPS and advanced routing. Unlocks analytics features and higher SLA.
2) Seat + add-on (keep Standard, buy "High Throughput" add-on + 30 seats) —
   lower monthly commitment, keeps per-token pricing similar. Works well if
   extra capacity is intermittent.
3) Hybrid (reserve burst capacity for nightly jobs + Standard daily capacity) —
   commit to 6-month reserved burst; pay per-use outside burst windows.

Migration credit: we can offer a one-time migration credit equal to 1 month of
Standard plan list price against a 12-month prepaid commitment (subject to
approval). For blended discounts: we typically tier discounts by committed $
volume on the 12-month term; for temporary higher-tier windows we can create a
temporary add-on discount schedule in the SOW.

I attached bundle_pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx with example numbers. If helpful, can
set up an internal call with Ben (pricing) and Priyom (entitlements) to finalize
options and draft a simple SOW.

Next step: do you want the 30k RPS nightly window modeled (I saw that in the
PDF) or should we use a conservative 15k window for the example?

Thanks,
Tessa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Emma / Kevin — apologies for the slight delay. We've hashed out the three
paths, and below is a concise recommendation with cost deltas and next steps.

Recommendation (short): Given WellWorks' profile (two critical inference
pipelines, intermittent large nightly batch), we recommend the route-scoped add-on
with a 12-month term + 3-month promotional discount. This minimizes ongoing
commitment while giving predictable nightly capacity.

Option A — Tier lift (Standard -> Premium)
- Who it's for: customers wanting all Premium features across the board.
- Impact: immediate access to enhanced routing, analytics, and higher SLA.
- Price delta: ~+40% ARR vs current Standard baseline (example model in sheet).
- Pros: simplest entitlement model. Cons: higher sustained cost.

Option B — Route-scoped High Throughput add-on (recommended)
- Who it's for: customers who need premium performance for select pipelines.
- Structure: 12-month commitment; reserve a nightly burst pool (2 hours @ 30k
  RPS) + standard daily capacity.
- Promo: 20% off add-on for first 3 months; one-time migration credit equal to
  1 month of Standard list if they prepay 12 months.
- Price delta: ~+18-22% ARR (with promo and credit amortized).
- Pros: cost-efficient, targeted. Cons: slightly more complex SOW.

Option C — Hybrid reserved burst model (short-term reserves + on-demand)
- Who it's for: teams testing scale or with heavy seasonal spikes.
- Structure: 6-month reserved burst with optional extension.
- Price delta: variable; typically +12-28% depending on committed hours.

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether you'd prefer the 30k RPS nightly target or we model 15k
   as a conservative baseline.
2) If Option B looks good, I'll route a clean SOW + pricing worksheet and a
   one-page memo for procurement. Ben will join the SOW review for technical
   entitlements; Priyom will add the add-on gating language.
3) We can schedule a 30-min pricing alignment call this week (Ben, Priyom 
   optional).

If you want, Laura can prepare a version of the SOW with the pilot promo
embedded so procurement can see the invoice schedule.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
